name: Da Beatminerz
sources: Passion of the Weiss — "We're samplers so we listen to everything": interview with Da Beatminerz (https://www.passionweiss.com/2024/04/02/da-beatminerz-mr-walt-dj-evil-dee-interview-stifled-creativity/)
notes: Brooklyn's murkiest kit, and the research names the defining parameter outright: "enormous filtered sample bass, sustained, dominating the mix". Everything else in this model is arranged around that. The melody sits high — [67,89], the highest register on this axis — because the research says a single organ or horn phrase sits *high above the bass*, and the drums go the other way: `velocityTiers` is lowered across the board for a snare "buried in low-mid", the hats stop being continuous, and the kick carries a raised sub layer. ⚠ **The bass is `mirror_kick`, not a held note, and that is an engine limit rather than a reading of the record.** `reese_sustain` is the only rhythm that holds a note and it emits one note per chord — over a static i that is one note per loop, which measured 8 distinct basslines in 1000 seeds. `mirror_kick` over a kick that plays 1 and 3& gives two very low roots a bar, which reads as sustained at 91 BPM, and `followRootsProb` 0.94 keeps it on the tonic. ⚠ `hihat.continuous` is false because the research says the hats are sparse; `fillDensity` is 0.3 rather than lower because a model that declares a hat block owes every seed a hat. ⚠ `medium` because the research rates it medium-high — sourcing and processing are first-person, drum numbers are not. The specific inferred parameter is `velocityTiers`: "buried in low-mid" is a mix description this model translates into velocity, which is the only lever a MIDI style model has. ⚠ The i–iv and i–VII families are INFERRED — the research names static i only — and both carry low weights. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 917 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: densityRatio 0.45. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [1,2,4], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count.
